newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS - Tech shares to stay at fore of Taiwan rally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Tech shares to stay at fore of Taiwan rally.

text.p: High-flying electronics have emerged as the sector to carry Taiwan's volatile stock market, which has risen some 100 percent since China test-fired missiles onto the island's doorstep in March 1996.
The technology index rose 111 percent in the first half of 1997, compared with just 25.4 percent in all of 1996, reflecting the industry's strong performance and promising prospects.
The sector's ascent has not been smooth.
Taiwan technology shares nosedived some 15 percent on heavy profit-taking between July 17-23, only to recover 6.56 percent on Thursday on a technical rebound.
Forty-three of the big board's 62 technology shares, chip giant Taiwan Semiconductor among them, flirted with the daily seven percent limit on Thursday, brokers said.
Once the dust settled, brokers said the heavily weighted electronics sector alone had added 190 points to a 251-point, 2.68-percent rise on the main index, which ended at 9,632.42.

Tech shares have been the single most important motor behind the rough doubling of the main index in the 16 months since rival China's military menacing of Taiwan sent stock market funds fleeing into foreign exchange, gold and other safe havens.
Analysts nonetheless cautioned that a speculative undercurrent in electronics could undermine the sector's healthy growth -- and threaten the wider market's performance.
"With electronics becoming so red-hot, a speculative trend in the sector is inevitable," said Ben Lee of Nomura Securities. "This is not healthy for the sector's long-term growth."
Brokers said electronics had clearly pushed aside Taiwan's heavily weighted financials, which had dominated the market for years.
But are the fundamentals in the technology sector really that strong? Can the industry sustain such performance?
President Securities assistant manager Alan Yeh says yes.
"This is something beyond doubt," Yeh told Reuters. "Over 60 percent of daily stock turnover now comes from electronics."
That's a significant statistic in a market where turnover regularly eclipses T$200 billion (US$7.2 billion) and rocketed to a historic high T$297 billion (US$10.6 billion) on July 17.

The electronic industry with its burgeoning earnings has emerged as the island's star industry in recent years, long since stealing the proud "Made in Taiwan" mantle from shoes, garments, bicycles and umbrellas.

State statistics showed the sector chalked up well over 15 percent -- or US$1.71 billion -- of a total US$10.36 billion in foreign orders for Taiwan goods in June, a 9.3 percent rise compared to June 1996.
Despite such growth, brokers say investors have begun to consider some electronics shares overpriced as share prices have risen far faster than profits.
"This explains why there has been a sustained sell-off in the electronic sector by institutional investors in recent sessions," Lin Long-hsien of United Securities said.
Concerns about overpricing prompted regulators on Tuesday to publicly urge accountants to be particularly rigorous when reviewing the earnings reports of technology companies.

Market-watchers say they are not worried, forecasting that Taiwan's good industrial long-term fundamentals bode well for a continued rise in the stock market -- with technology shares leading the way.
Economics minister Wang Chih-kang said on Tuesday that the island would have no trouble reaching its target of gross domestic product growing by 6.24 percent in 1998.
"The only thing investors should be cautious about is how to prevent all funds from pouring into the electronics sector," said Nomura's Lee.
